subject: Reasoning
description: Eligibility filters: candidate fits / fails / referred / pending — bank-PO style

questions.stem: ELIGIBILITY: candidate must (a) be 21-30 years (b) have minimum 60% in graduation (c) speak Hindi + English. Ravi: 25 yrs, 65% grad, knows only English. Decision:
questions.explanation: Ravi: age ✓ (25 in 21-30); marks ✓ (65 ≥ 60); language ✗ (knows ONLY English; needs both). REJECTED on language. METHOD: read each criterion as a CHECKLIST; ANY fail → reject. ALL pass → select. INSIGHT — these questions test careful reading + attention to 'AND' vs 'OR' joins. 'Speak Hindi AND English' = both required; 'Hindi OR English' = either suffices. PYQ TRAP: candidates may meet 4/5 criteria — STILL reject if any one fails. ESCAPE valves — 'referred' / 'pending' — used only when problem explicitly says so (e.g., narrow miss on a specific criterion).

questions.stem: Same criteria. Priya: 22 yrs, 58% grad, knows Hindi + English. Decision:
questions.explanation: Age ✓; language ✓; marks 58 < 60 ✗ → REJECT. INSIGHT: cut-off marks are STRICT — even 0.5% below cuts you out. Real-life: many bank PO + civil service exams have rigid cut-offs. PRACTICAL TIP for problems: write each criterion as a column, mark ✓/✗; if all ✓, select. Sometimes problems have a 'deviation rule' like 'marks shortfall ≤ 2% can be referred to higher authority' — in such cases, 58% (i.e., 2% below) might be referred. Always re-read the deviation clauses carefully.

questions.stem: Same criteria. Amit: 24 yrs, 75% grad, knows Hindi + English + Tamil. Decision:

options.option_text: Rejected because he knows extra languages

questions.explanation: Age ✓; marks ✓ (75 ≥ 60); language ✓ (knows H+E, plus EXTRA Tamil — more languages don't disqualify; only NOT having required ones does). SELECT. INSIGHT — criteria are MINIMUM thresholds; exceeding them is fine. TYPICAL TRAP: students see 'extra' qualifications + reject — wrong. Read criteria as 'must include X' not 'must include ONLY X'. Same as job ads: 'minimum 5 years experience' = 5 OR more. Same in age range '21-30': 21 + 30 ARE included (inclusive boundaries by default unless 'between' is strict).

questions.stem: Loan eligibility: applicant must (a) have a stable job for 2+ yrs, (b) earn ≥ ₹40,000/month, (c) have credit score ≥ 750. Sneha: stable job 3 yrs, earns ₹35K/month, score 780. Decision:
questions.explanation: Job ✓; credit score ✓ (780 ≥ 750); income 35K < 40K ✗ → REJECT. INSIGHT: in real lending, ALL criteria are AND-joined; banks don't trade off (they may approve at higher rate sometimes, but per the problem rules, fail = reject). REAL-WORLD INSIGHT: credit scores in India range 300-900 (CIBIL); 750+ = good; 800+ = excellent. INCOME-to-EMI ratio (FOIR) typically capped at 50% by banks. STABLE JOB requirement = job stability proxy for repayment continuity. Decision-making questions mirror real bank-PO judgment work.

questions.stem: School admission: child needs to be (a) age 5-6 yrs, (b) have proof of vaccination. ALSO 'if child is 4 yrs but has elder sibling already in school, refer to principal'. Riya: 4 yrs, vaccinated, has elder sibling in school. Decision:

options.option_text: Rejected because she is too young

questions.explanation: Riya is 4 (BELOW age range 5-6) → would normally REJECT. BUT deviation clause: 'if 4 yrs AND elder sibling in school → REFER to principal'. Both deviation conditions met → REFER. INSIGHT — DEVIATION clauses are 'escape valves' built into eligibility rules to handle edge cases (siblings, special circumstances). Read EXACTLY: 'AND' means both must hold; 'OR' = either. Common SSC framework: criteria → exception → exception's own conditions. This is also how real-world bureaucratic rules work — first-tier rules + waiver clauses for special cases.

questions.stem: Driving license: applicant must (a) be ≥ 18 yrs, (b) pass driving test, (c) submit photo + ID proof. Ramesh: 19, passed test, submitted photo BUT no ID proof. Decision:
questions.explanation: Age ✓; test ✓; ID proof ✗ → REJECT (or PEND till submitted). INSIGHT — DOCUMENTARY criteria are non-negotiable, even if other 'merit' criteria pass. REAL: India's RTO won't issue license without complete documentation; same for any official process. PRACTICAL TAKEAWAY: in real exams these questions reward CHECKLIST DISCIPLINE — go through each criterion mechanically, don't skip. 'If candidate fails to provide a single document → application incomplete = rejected'. Applies to bank account opening, passport, gas connection, etc. Same logic in business: a contract isn't binding without all required signatures.

questions.stem: Bank PO selection: candidate needs (a) 60%+ in grad, (b) 21-30 yrs, (c) cleared written exam. EXCEPTION: SC/ST candidates get 5% relaxation in marks. Mohan (SC): 56% grad, 24 yrs, cleared exam. Decision:

options.option_text: Referred to higher authority for review
Data insufficient to decide today option

questions.explanation: EXCEPTION: SC/ST get 5% relaxation → effective minimum = 55%. Mohan SC, 56% ≥ 55% ✓; age ✓; cleared ✓ → SELECT. INSIGHT — RESERVATION + RELAXATION clauses are common in Indian recruitment. SC/ST often get: 5% marks relaxation, age relaxation (5 yrs), reservation in seats (15% SC + 7.5% ST in central jobs). OBC: 27% reservation; some marks/age relaxation. EWS: 10% reservation since 2019 (103rd Amendment). PRACTICAL: read EXCEPTIONS BEFORE applying main criteria — exceptions trump base rules for those they cover. Also called 'caveat' clauses in legal language.
